questions.q: Why does the lesson say a model's deployment-time accuracy is 'a claim about one moment in time, not a permanent guarantee'?
options: Because the model's code changes automatically after deployment
Because test set accuracy is always calculated incorrectly
Because the real world keeps changing after deployment — customer behavior, fraud patterns, or market conditions can shift without any change to the model's code
Because deployment-time accuracy is never a real measurement to begin with
questions.explain: A trained model is a frozen snapshot of training-time patterns; the real world around it keeps changing, so deployment-time accuracy doesn't guarantee future accuracy.

questions.q: What is data drift, as defined in this lesson?
options: A measurable drop in the model's actual predictive performance, requiring ground-truth labels to detect
A change in the statistical distribution of input data in production compared to training data, detectable without necessarily waiting for performance to drop
A permanent, irreversible failure of the model serving infrastructure
A change in the GPU hardware used to serve the model
questions.explain: Data drift (feature drift/covariate shift) is a shift in input feature distributions, detected with tests like Kolmogorov-Smirnov or PSI, independent of whether performance has visibly dropped yet.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say data drift is often an earlier warning sign than model drift?
options: Model drift can be detected instantly with no data at all
Data drift only matters for models trained on GPUs
Data drift requires more compute to detect than model drift
Model drift requires ground-truth labels, which often arrive on a delay, while data drift can be measured directly from live input features without waiting for labels
questions.explain: Model drift needs confirmed outcomes (ground-truth labels) that can take days to arrive, while data drift can be measured immediately by comparing live input distributions to the training baseline.

questions.q: Which of the following is listed as something a real production monitoring setup tracks?
options: Only the original training script's line count
Per-feature input distribution checks, prediction distribution shifts, performance metrics against delayed ground truth, and serving infrastructure health
The office location of the data science team
Only the model's file size on disk
questions.explain: The lesson lists input distribution checks, prediction distribution monitoring, performance metrics recalculated as labels arrive, and operational health (latency/error rates) from the serving layer.

questions.q: How does a drift alert close the loop with the CI/CD pipeline from Lesson 19?
options: A drift alert fires the retraining trigger directly (the repository_dispatch event), starting the automated retrain-evaluate-promote cycle
A drift alert has no connection to the CI/CD pipeline described in Lesson 19
A drift alert automatically deletes the current production model with no retraining
A drift alert only sends an email and takes no automated pipeline action
questions.explain: The drift alert is exactly the repository_dispatch trigger from lesson 19's pipeline — monitoring detects the problem, and the CI/CD pipeline retrains, gates, and promotes automatically if the new model clears the bar.
